review.evidence: Issue #4213 clearly documents the defect: indexing `x[:a, :b]` on a 1-dimensional DenseAxisArray throws `MethodError: no method matching one(::Symbol)` instead of a useful error. PR #4215 closes this issue. The commit modifies production files (DenseAxisArray.jl, SparseAxisArray.jl) and adds corresponding tests. The fix addresses existing broken behavior (incorrect/confusing error) rather than adding new functionality.
review.missing_evidence: The actual diff content is not provided, so the exact nature of the fix (whether it throws a better error or handles the indexing differently) cannot be inspected directly. However, issue context and file changes strongly suggest a targeted bug fix.
suggested_tests: Test that indexing a 1-D DenseAxisArray with multiple indices throws a clear DimensionMismatch or BoundsError rather than MethodError
Test that indexing a SparseAxisArray with wrong number of dimensions gives a useful error

review.summary: Fix for a confusing MethodError when indexing a DenseAxisArray/SparseAxisArray with the wrong number of dimensions. Instead of an opaque 'no method matching one(::Symbol)' error, a more useful error message is provided. This is a bug fix per the 'method error principle' — the original behavior produced an unhelpful internal error rather than a meaningful user-facing error.
review.validation_risks: The fix may be primarily an improved error message rather than a change in computational behavior, which borders on diagnostic-only. However, since the original behavior was a confusing internal MethodError (effectively a crash with wrong error type), converting it to a proper bounds/dimension error is a legitimate behavior fix.
